title: BEG-06 noise-area breakout (SPY/QQQ) rule-18 rework: wider stop, band, check step, one entry a day (8 configs)
mechanism: Index ETFs that leave the 14-day average intraday noise band on the side of VWAP keep trending (Zarattini/Aziz/Barbon 2024). Falsified if <= 0 after costs or no better than random sides.
hypothesis: The near miss failed because costs (~0.10R a trade at a 0.25 x ATR stop) eat a real pre-cost directional edge; a wider stop, a different band or fewer checks lowers cost per R without losing the edge.
notes: Tested 2026-11-21 (research/bdi/1121/rework, bench10 normal way via the beginner runner, LR8 + borrow, testing-arena book; locked block not read; PLAN.md pre-registered). FIT avg R (n): base -0.095 (265), notrail -0.083 (217), R6a stop 0.375 -0.095 (197), R6b stop 0.50 -0.061 (187), R6c stop 0.375+trail -0.080 (259), R6d band 1.25 -0.096 (176), R6e band 0.75 -0.073 (271), R6f hourly checks +0.003 (166, w/o best day -0.092, best day 2025-04-09), R6g one entry -0.162 (171), R6h stop 0.375+band 1.25 -0.069 (157). Wider stops cut gross R as much as cost (R6a gross -0.021 vs +0.029). FIT pick R6f -> CHECK (look 3, bar t 2.0) -0.088 (n 331, t -0.93, w/o best day -0.127, w/o top 2 -0.159; QQQ -0.008 / SPY -0.162; flat-SPY days -0.90): FAIL, worse than the beginner pick notrail (CHECK -0.013). Lineage 12 configs, 3 CHECK looks used. Salvage: none as a setup; the only stable fact is QQQ > SPY in every window (not tested as a rule, seen on CHECK).

title: BEG-04 quiet gap fade rule-18 rework: closer target, wider stop, relaxed 1.2R test, rvol filter removed, gap 2.0% (8 configs)
mechanism: Quiet (low relative volume) 1.5-6% gaps fill toward the prior close once the first 20-minute range breaks against the gap. Falsified if <= 0 after costs or no better than random fade entries on universe days.
hypothesis: The near miss failed because the trigger is late (much of the fill already done) and the day choice carries the edge; a closer target or wider stop should keep more of the fill.
notes: Tested 2026-11-21 (research/bdi/1121/rework, bench10 normal way via the beginner runner's own functions; T1 day table rebuilt with the BEG-02 build code; base FIT parity exact 1,860 / +0.1062; locked block not read; PLAN.md pre-registered; T2 not run). FIT avg R (n, w/o best day): base +0.106 (1860, -0.001; 2025-04-08 = 100% of FIT R), R4a tgt 0.5 -0.043 (319), R4b tgt 0.75 +0.132 (1082, +0.023), R4c min R 0.8 +0.033 (2947), R4d stop x1.5 +0.039 (981), R4e ATR cap 0.5 +0.060 (1467), R4f rvol filter off +0.106 (3091, -0.004), R4g gap >= 2.0% +0.185 (1409, +0.046), R4h tgt 0.5 + stop x1.5 -0.222 (111). Every FIT figure is the April-2025 tariff week. FIT pick R4g -> CHECK (look 3) -0.034 (n 3375, t -0.42, w/o best day -0.087, w/o top 2 -0.124; shorts -0.082 / longs +0.007; best days 2026-04-02 +170R, 2025-11-20 +111R): FAIL the pass; NEAR vs the top-10 standard (CHECK w/o best day misses -0.078 by 0.009) - the same place as gap25. Lineage 12, 3 CHECK looks used. Salvage: the long (gap-down fill) leg is ~0 on CHECK; the edge, if any, is in which days fill, not in the trigger, target or stop.

title: GC1/GC2: correlated-group lot cap - symbols with FIT daily-return correlation >= 0.85 count as one symbol for the per-setup lot cap (1 or 2 lots per group)
hypothesis: Give-back 11-20: NM-ETF-late-dip-di-long opened 12 correlated ETF lots in 14:11-14:16 ET (three bets taken twelve times), all stopped, -12.6R; capping near-duplicate lots should cut that without touching uncorrelated trades.
notes: Tested 2026-11-21 on the 11-19 top-10 benchmark T1 signals (bench10 normal way, home-account books; FIT/CHECK; 2 configs; PLAN.md pre-registered). FAIL both. NM-ETF itself (the target): GC1 FIT -38.6R (kept 54%), CHECK -6.6R; GC2 FIT -31.6R, CHECK -0.6R - its stacked late dips are its best two-year trades. Across 11 setups: GC1 CHECK 5 better (+109.4R) / 6 worse (-49.3R), total +60.2R but almost all from cutting 40% of L3-fromopen (top-decile winners kept 44%; gain below every random-removal draw); GC2 CHECK 2 better (+25.5R) / 9 worse (-40.0R), total -14.5R. Live week replay (descriptive): GC1 would have blocked 57 Primary lots (+4.0R), GC2 26 lots (+6.4R; 11-20 NM-ETF +6.2R). Same verdict as BURST1/2, sat1114 G1-G4 and giveback_1119: trading less of a stack is not an edge.

title: Peer-group cluster, laggard follows: when >= 3 members of one industry group are already >= 0.5 ATR the same way at 09:50, trade the members that have not moved yet (same side)
mechanism: Day type: an industry-level shock (policy, peer earnings, guidance) is visible by 09:50 as >= 3 group members moving together. Reason (falsifiable): institutional repricing of the group reaches the less-covered members with a lag. Falsified if laggards entered at 09:50 do no better than the same names on non-cluster days, or <= 0 after costs.
hypothesis: Move Hunt 11-17..11-20: managed care moved as one group (11-18 UNH, HUM, ELV, MOH, CNC, CVS all top-25 shorts, decided 09:35-09:40; 11-19 CI, UNH; also 11-02, 11-06, 11-11, 11-12 in the library). No live setup trades sector-shock laggards.
test_needed: E2 2-year screen (lab frames + gates) with a point-in-time industry map; pre-register group size, threshold, laggard definition; report overlap with parked mh-1102-open-group-move (which traded the group itself, 16 configs failed); ETB short universe.
notes: Filed from the BD&I Saturday Move Hunt scan (research/bdi/1121/scan/NOTES.md); untested.

title: Crypto complex follows bitcoin: when the spot-BTC ETFs are already >= 0.75 ATR from the prior close at 09:50, trade the lagging crypto ETFs / miners the same way (long-only via inverse crypto ETPs on down days)
mechanism: Day type: bitcoin's overnight move (it trades 24h) shows up at the open in IBIT/FBTC. Reason (falsifiable): crypto ETFs, miners and leveraged / inverse crypto ETPs reprice to the same underlying with different speed. Falsified if lagging members at 09:50 do no better than the same names at 10:00 on non-trigger days, or <= 0 after costs.
hypothesis: Move Hunt: 11-20 IBIT, FBTC, GBTC, BITO, ETHA top-25 shorts and MSTZ, BTCZ (inverse) top-25 longs; 11-19 MSTZ; miners MARA, CLSK, RIOT on 11-03 / 11-10 / 11-12 (12 library rows on 5 days, 33% caught vs 5% for all moves). Not the cap-etp family (index inverse / vol ETPs, do-not-re-run in research/final1121).
test_needed: E2 2-year screen; pre-registered list of crypto ETFs / miners / crypto ETPs present in the lab; trigger on IBIT (or GBTC before 2024-01) at 09:50; random-entry and 10:00 controls; ETB for shorts.
notes: Filed from the BD&I Saturday Move Hunt scan (research/bdi/1121/scan/NOTES.md); untested.

title: Defensive relative strength on weak opens: SPY <= -0.30% at 09:50 -> buy low-beta defensives (utilities / staples / REITs) that are above their open and above VWAP
mechanism: Day type: SPY down at 09:50. Reason (falsifiable): de-risking rotates money into low-beta defensives the same morning. Falsified if these longs do no better than the same names on SPY-up opens, or <= 0 after costs, or if they only win on days SPY recovers (a beta bet).
hypothesis: Long-side capture was 1 of 100 big long moves 11-17..11-20; several long movers were defensives (11-17 CPB, EIX on a SPY-down open; 11-18 EGP, CTRE). Mirror of parked mh-1106-defensive-rotation-0950 (up opens), whose only positive pocket was down-close days (+0.158R).
test_needed: E2 2-year screen; 60-day beta lagged one session (as mh_p1.py); report R by SPY open->close day type to show it is not a recovery bet; compare with mh-1106.
notes: Filed from the BD&I Saturday Move Hunt scan (research/bdi/1121/scan/NOTES.md); untested.
